claims.explanation: Monastrol selectively kills cancer cell lines that are highly dependent on KIF11 (Eg5) for mitotic spindle assembly, likely due to increased KIF11 expression or mutations that disrupt mitotic checkpoints, making cells more sensitive to monopolar spindle-induced arrest. Lines with functional p53 and intact spindle assembly checkpoint may undergo apoptosis more readily upon prolonged mitotic arrest, while those with mutations in TP53 or other checkpoint genes may be less sensitive. Additionally, mutations in genes such as KRAS, BRAF, and PTEN may modulate sensitivity through effects on proliferation and survival signaling.

features.basis: Higher expression of the drug target increases dependence and sensitivity to inhibition.
Loss of p53 may impair apoptotic response to mitotic arrest, reducing sensitivity.
KRAS mutations are common in sensitive lines and may drive proliferation, increasing reliance on mitosis.
BRAF mutations are observed in several sensitive lines and may promote mitotic entry.
PTEN loss is seen in sensitive lines and may enhance PI3K/AKT signaling, supporting proliferation.
RB1 mutations appear in sensitive lines and may deregulate cell cycle checkpoints.
CDKN2A loss is present in some sensitive lines and may lead to unchecked proliferation.
ATM mutations are found in sensitive lines and may impair DNA damage response, increasing mitotic catastrophe.
ARID1A mutations appear in sensitive lines and may alter chromatin remodeling, affecting mitotic gene expression.
KMT2D mutations are common in sensitive lines and may impact epigenetic regulation of mitosis.
EGFR mutations are seen in some sensitive lung lines and may drive proliferation.
SF3B1 mutations appear in sensitive lines and may affect splicing of mitotic regulators.
